title: If You Want to Go Fast, Go Alone
subtitle: Individual effort may move quickly, but lasting progress requires others.
author: Murle Connect Editorial Team
proverb: If you want to go fast, go alone; if you want to go far, go together.
summary: This proverb contrasts speed with endurance and explains that individual effort may produce quick results, while lasting achievements require cooperation, patience, trust, and shared responsibility. Its message reflects the importance of community, collective effort, and mutual support in overcoming long and difficult journeys.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Human beings often desire quick success. A person may want to complete a task immediately, reach a destination quickly, or achieve a goal without waiting for others. However, many of the most important journeys in life are too difficult to complete alone. This proverb reminds us that speed and distance are not the same. Moving quickly may be useful for a short task, but reaching a meaningful and lasting destination often requires cooperation.

sections.heading: Meaning
sections.content: The proverb presents two different paths. Going alone may allow a person to make decisions quickly because there is no need to consult others or coordinate different opinions. However, working alone also means carrying every responsibility alone. Going together may take more time because people must discuss, plan, listen, compromise, and support one another. Yet a group can endure challenges that would overwhelm one individual. The deeper message is that long-term success depends more on unity than on speed.

sections.heading: Traditional Story
sections.content: A traveler once decided to cross a difficult stretch of land alone because he believed that moving without companions would make him faster. At first, he walked quickly and felt proud of his progress. Later, he became tired, lost his direction, and struggled to find water and shelter. Another group traveling behind him moved more slowly because they consulted one another and shared their supplies. When one person became weak, the others supported him. Although the group arrived later, they reached the destination safely together. The story teaches that the fastest beginning does not always lead to the strongest ending.

sections.heading: Lesson
sections.content: The proverb teaches patience, cooperation, and the importance of shared responsibility. It warns against selfishness and the belief that personal ability is always enough. A person may be talented, but talent becomes more powerful when combined with the skills of others. The lesson is not that people should never work alone. Instead, it teaches that major goals involving families, communities, development, peace, and cultural preservation require collective participation.

sections.heading: Modern Application
sections.content: This proverb applies to education, business, community development, leadership, family life, and cultural preservation. A student may study alone, but teachers and classmates can provide guidance. An entrepreneur may begin with a personal idea, but a strong team can help the idea grow. A community cannot build lasting peace if every person acts only for themselves. For Murle society, preserving language, history, traditions, and oral knowledge requires elders, parents, researchers, teachers, artists, and young people to work together.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.content: Going alone may sometimes be necessary for a short distance, but going together is essential for a long journey. Cooperation creates strength, shared knowledge, emotional support, and resilience. The proverb reminds people that meaningful progress is not measured only by how quickly one person moves, but by how many people can safely and successfully reach the destination together.

moral: Quick progress may come through individual effort, but lasting success is achieved through unity, patience, and cooperation.
reflection: Are you trying to reach an important goal alone when cooperation with others could help you go farther?
